To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a classification system that takes as input a private household's electricity consumption traces and provides as output an estimate of its properties of interest.
CLASS can automatically estimate properties of private households with high accuracy and can leverage a priori information to increase its accuracy.

CLASS can be used to estimate household properties with more that 70% accuracy using electricity consumption data only and that for selected properties, the accuracy can be increased up to 11% when using additional a priori information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a system that can be used by energy providers to classify households according their socio-economic status.
the automatic estimation of properties of private households based on electricity consumption data and provides a system that is capable of doing so.
the use of electricity consumption data of households to automatically infer socio-economic properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a combination of a priori and a posteriori information can increase the classification accuracy by up 20%.
the proposed classification approach is a promising starting point to automatically derive socio-economic properties of private households using their electricity consumption data.
CLASS is a useful tool that allows to estimate household properties with high accuracy, even if the classification is based on electricity consumption data alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CLASS is a promising approach to automatically classify households according to their socio-economic properties, using electricity consumption data only or in combination with a priori knowledge.
electricity consumption data is a rich source of knowledge about private households.
electricity consumption data can be used to automatically estimate properties of private households.
The main takeaway from our work is that

electricity consumption data can be leveraged to estimate socio-economic household properties, which can be used for a variety of purposes, such as the design of tailored premium services for energy consumers.
